not_legal_advice: An opinion by an agent, not legal advice. Whether something is lawful, or what a platform will accept, is for a lawyer or the platform. No model was used for these opinions (counsel.d's OpenRouter line waits on Dinis), so none is 'reviewed by models'.

reasons: Does a browser-only app escape the yearly CASA assessment? Google's page does not say so. It ties the assessment to an app that 'has the ability to access data from or through a third-party server' (also: 'if the app accesses or has the capability to access Google user data from or through a server'), and adds 'It is your responsibility to understand and determine your application type', or leave it to 'The Google API's verification team'. A browser-only design is the best case for arguing no assessment applies, but it is an argument, not an exemption, and Google decides.

If the backups land in a vault hosted on a server we run, even encrypted, the Gmail data arguably passes 'through a third-party server'. That weakens the browser-only argument for b); it is the main reason to keep Gmail off our app for now.

So a) is the safer split: Calendar on our app (sensitive scope: Google review, 'can take up to 10 days', brand verification first), Gmail on each owner's own app, where Google's 'Personal use' exception fits ('you are the only user of your app or if your app is used by only a few users, all of whom are known personally to you'), with its user cap.
d) is consistent: a free demo with no sign-up and no price makes no commercial promise.
conditions: C1. The Google verification is Dinis's own act: submitting the app, the consent screen, the privacy-policy link and the scope justifications are statements to Google and acceptance of its policies, which no agent makes for him (R14). Agents prepare; Dinis submits.

C2. Before submission, a privacy policy for the demo that is true to the design (what is read, where it goes, that tokens stay in memory, that backups go only to the owner's vault, how to revoke), since Google's verification checks 'accurate OAuth consent screen information and policy links'. counsel.d to review the draft.
C3. Least scopes: read-only Calendar for the demo; no Gmail scope on our app until Dinis decides b) with accountant.b's written figure (as accountant.b says).
C4. The demo page says it is a demo, that Google's own unverified-app or consent screens are Google's, and makes no claim that Google has approved anything until it has.
C5. security.b's conditions stand (tokens in memory only, backups only into the owner's vault, connect-src exact Google hosts).
C6. Each owner's own Gmail app is the owner's own arrangement with Google: our guide to setting one up says so and promises nothing about Google's treatment of it.
items.disagreements_or_uncertainty: Uncertain, not settled by any page read: whether Google treats a browser-only restricted-scope app with an operator-hosted encrypted vault as 'through a third-party server'. To settle before any move to b): ask Google's verification team (a person sends it) or a lawyer.
